gamespot.com/articles/one-day-out-from-e.title: One Day Out From Early Access, Emberville Has Been Delayed To 2027
gamespot.com/articles/one-day-out-from-e.excerpt: Originally set to enter early access on October 27, action-adventure RPG Emberville has been delayed by over two months to January 7, 2027. The last-minute delay gives the team time to make "essential improvements" before Emberville reaches its fans. The upcoming game mixes Stardew Valley-like farming and community building with action-adventure RPG combat. Trapped in a magical underground dungeon, the player must uncover the truth about their cursed prison while revitalizing the ruined town of Emberville. Emberville's demo was one of the most played during Steam Next Fest last week; however, player feedback from the demo has led to a last-minute delay. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sOJmwxZZsX0 "Some of the improvements we want to make are systems changes that can't be done quickly," the Emberville team said , acknowledging feedback from Next Fest players. "Reworking bow combat, for example, would take more time than we had prior to our Early Access release even though the team is working around the clock. After carefully considering our options, we have decided to move the release date and include some essential improvements in the Early Access launch build." While the game is intended to grow and improve throughout its early access period, with the developer planning to add new content incrementally, the studio wants to reach a certain baseline before it launches. "Our team has a clear vision for how Emberville will develop throughout early access," the Steam post continues. "On January 7, our goal is to deliver an experience that shows what makes the game distinctive, establishes its core gameplay, and offers a compelling glimpse of how the game will grow throughout early access." While some players are disappointed by the eleventh-hour delay, others have said they're happy for the Emberville team to take as much time as it needs to get the game up to scratch. gamespot.com/articles/ghost-of-yotei-was.title: Ghost Of Yotei Was A Hit, But Its Developer Is Reportedly Cutting Jobs
gamespot.com/articles/ghost-of-yotei-was.excerpt: Sony-owned studio Sucker Punch Productions is losing 24 employees in another round of layoffs in the games industry. The studio is behind Ghost of Tsushima and Ghost of Yotei , two first-party PlayStation titles that have been critical and commercial hits . An Aftermath report claims 24 Sucker Punch staff have lost their jobs. The studio is estimated to have between 190 and 230 staff, depending on the source, meaning Sucker Punch has lost at least 10% of its employees. "After carefully observing the challenges in the market and reviewing the team needs for our next project, we've decided to make some staffing reductions," an email from studio leadership quoted by Aftermath read. "Several positions across Sucker Punch will be eliminated as a result." "We know this is a lot to take in, and we want to assure you that we did not make this decision lightly. We have given this a lot of attention and worked to support our affected colleagues during this transition as well as we can," the email continued, adding: "Next week we will go into more details about the future." https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d48IWwIRg98 For the past decade, Sucker Punch has worked on its two open-world samurai adventure games, both standout successes in Sony's first-party slate. As of 2022, Ghost of Tsushima had sold over 8 million lifetime copies , while Ghost of Yotei was reported to be Sony's best-selling title on the PS5 as of June 2026. The studio's latest release was the critically acclaimed Echoes of Sekigahara expansion for Ghost of Yotei, which brought back the first game's protagonist, Jin Sakai. Prior to Ghost of Tsushima, Sucker Punch developed the Sly Cooper and Infamous series. This isn't the first time the studio has undergone layoffs after a commercially successful release; an unspecified number of layoffs occurred in 2014 following the launch of Infamous Second Son, the same month the expansion First Light was released.

gamespot.com/articles/elden-ring-movie-m.title: Elden Ring Movie Might Be Extremely Long, And It Could Have Twitch Integration Eventually
gamespot.com/articles/elden-ring-movie-m.excerpt: New details have come to light about A24's Elden Ring movie, including how Amazon could be involved and its beefy runtime. According to Deadline , Amazon MGM is buying up the Elden Ring movie's Pay-1 streaming rights for numerous international markets in a deal potentially worth "tens of millions of dollars." The site reported that there could be "interesting activations" on Amazon's Twitch platform as part of the deal. A Pay-1 rights deal means the company gets exclusive rights to broadcast a movie after it ends its theatrical run and comes to home video. Netflix, for example, paid Sony billions of dollars for a Pay-1 deal that includes the live-action Zelda movie . That was a global deal for many movies, though, and the report said Amazon MGM is booking an international deal specifically for the Elden Ring movie. It remains to be seen where the Elden Ring movie could stream after it wraps up in theaters. The Elden Ring movie finished filming earlier this year and Industrial Light & Magic is now working on post-production efforts ahead of the movie's March 2028 release in theaters. The film is based on From Software's game and was written and directed by Alex Garland, but the story details are being kept secret. Kit Connor is playing the lead, and the movie will apparently feature "battles between his character and impressive monsters and dragons." The script is so secretive that A24 is reportedly booking flights for its staffers to potential international rights-buyers instead of sending the script digitally to ensure an A24 staffer is in the room as the script is being read. Additionally, the report said the script is at least 180 pages, meaning the film could stretch to a mighty three hours. It was also reported that Elden Ring could become a movie franchise if the film does well, but no sequel plans are officially set yet. gamespot.com/articles/check-out-46-secon.excerpt: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation aims to be the biggest chapter in the remake trilogy, not only in the number of regions players can explore, but also in verticality. Square Enix had previously shown off how the game's cast will be able to skydive into new locations on the world map, but for a taste of just how much verticality the game will have in certain areas, you can check out this new slice of gameplay set in the Midgar region, which features Cloud exploring a massive chasm underneath the city--and atop a pink chocobo, too. https://twitter.com/finalfantasyvii/status/2114720653161198074 While that's a lot of empty space to fly through, it's still impressive just how much of it there is. Of course, this is only one part of the game, and there's no guarantee every region will have caverns this massive. But considering how Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth greatly expanded on the environments of Final Fantasy 7 Remake with its open-world design, Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is expected to raise the bar by increasing the size of the world around Cloud and the rest of the gang. Revelation will also introduce Cid's iconic airship, the Highwind, which will serve as the gang's base of operations, and unfortunately, Chadley is there too. All that "planetary-scale" content will take up a lot of space on your PC or console, with game director Naoki Hamaguchi estimating the game will be "around" 200GB. One of the big games to look forward to next year, Final Fantasy 7 Revelation will launch on April 8, 2027. It's estimated that a complete playthrough could take as long as 100 hours--something Hamaguchi had done 46 times already when last we spoke to him--and two post-launch expansions starring Vincent Valentine and Sephiroth will follow in the game's wake. "My time with the final chapter of the Final Fantasy 7 remake trilogy clearly shows that the team at Square Enix has plenty of story left to tell. We’ll just have to wait until April for the rest of the Revelation(s)," Jason Fanelli wrote

gamespot.com/articles/valve-knows-steam-.title: Valve Knows Steam Next Fest Has An AI Slop Problem, And It’s Looking For Solutions
gamespot.com/articles/valve-knows-steam-.excerpt: Steam Next Fest has come and gone, and one of the big criticisms of the semi-regular showcase for game demos--aside from there being several thousand of them --was that there was simply too much AI slop floating to the top. Valve has responded to the feedback, and for now, its solution to avoiding hastily vibe-coded game demos is to simply be patient and wait a few days before diving in. Speaking at the Steam Indie Connect developer event (via Inven Global ), Tom Giardino and Marc Wilkinson from Valve's Steam Business Team addressed the recent criticisms of Next Fest. Wilkinson explained that users are shown a completely random lineup of game demos for the first two days of Next Fest, but after that time period, people can expect personalized recommendations to kick in. Wilkinson also added that many of the features about low-quality games surfacing were written during those first two days of Next Fest, although that doesn't change the fact that all those demos were still present for the duration of Next Fest. https://youtu.be/hRiAstgNtps As for why Next Fest starts off with a randomized selection of games, Wilkinson explained that it's done to give all developers equal exposure and to prevent system abuse. "We recognize that the trade-off is some low-quality games get exposed," Wilkinson said. "We are fully aware of the situation, and a significant number of people are thinking about how to solve this problem." As mentioned above, the other big problem with Next Fest was the sheer number of demos present, as the number has climbed sharply between Next Fest events. Giardino described this as "the pendulum swinging to the opposite side," as three years ago, there were "only 50 or 100 games" participating in Next Fest. rockpapershotgun.com/creation-without-a-.title: "Creation without a creator": Pathologic 3's devs have refused to patch an invisible apple tree, and for a blissful moment, I thought they were lying to poison Google's AI
rockpapershotgun.com/creation-without-a-.excerpt: Magnificent, depressing plague colony fable Pathologic 3 has received a sizeable game update that adds some new difficulty modes, a photo feature, and some new, worryingly folkloric methods of defeating a murky embodiment of disease. Developers Ice Pick Lodge have also staunchly refused to remove an invisible apple tree, describing this apparently "famous" bug as a hallmark of a game whose "symbolic nature has almost overtaken its function as a product". This appears to be the last major update for Pathologic 3, so that invisible apple tree is staying in the game forever. I confess, when I first read the Steam blog in question, I doubted. The thing about invisible apple trees is that they are quite easy to confuse with apple trees that are simply not there. Pathologic in general is a house of lies: as Quintin Smith (RPS in peace) put it in his legendary Butchering Pathologic trilogy , "absolutely everybody has an angle, everyone's bending the truth and trying to twist you round their fingers." Pathologic 3 especially is a purgatorial time travel story that must be continually rewritten, a crock of festering rumours enclosed by an enormous, phantom theatre. As such, I read Ice-Pick's typically professorial account of the "invisible apple tree" with intense suspicion. Read more

gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-online-could.title: GTA 6 Online Could Be Released In Early 2027, Bank Says
gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-online-could.excerpt: Take-Two's biggest release ever, GTA 6 , is coming up in November, but the company's share price continues to drop. It's down 21% this year and has now dipped under $200 this week after reaching a 52-week high of $265. In short, the stock is struggling , but one big bank says it sees a lot of upside, in part because Rockstar is expected to release a new version of GTA Online--potentially in the first quarter of 2027--that could generate loads of money. "We recommend being long $TTWO through the GTA 6 launch," the bank said in a memo to investors seen by Business Insider . Being "long" means the investor would buy and hold. The bank said Take-Two stock "remains cheap." In particular, Bank of America said investors are not fully appreciating how big GTA Online 2.0 could be. To be sure, Rockstar is calling GTA 6 a single-player game, but everyone expects multiplayer to arrive in some form eventually . GTA Online for GTA 5 has been, and continues to be, a huge moneymaker for Rockstar and Take-Two thanks to its many microtransactions. Many expect a new version of GTA Online for GTA 6 to up the ante even further and give players more reasons to spend time--and money--in the game. Bank of America said a new version of GTA Online for GTA 6 could launch in the first calendar quarter of 2027, meaning January-March. This is also around the time that a PC edition of GTA 6 could arrive , driving even more revenue. For comparison, both GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption II launched without online multiplayer support, so it would not be shocking if GTA 6 followed the same playbook. Bank of America has given Take-Two a "buy" rating and a price target of $330. That's below the company's previous $380 target, but still represents an upside of more than 60% based on the current stock price. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game's file size was recently revealed, and it's absolutely massive .

gamespot.com/articles/lotros-latest-expa.title: LOTRO’s Latest Expansion Is Out Now, Nearly 20 Years After The Game Launched
gamespot.com/articles/lotros-latest-expa.excerpt: The Lord of the Rings Online, an MMO based on the popular fantasy series, got its latest expansion today, some 19.5 years after the game was originally released in 2007. The new expansion is called The Wolves of Mordor, and as its name suggests, the expansion is focused on the werewolves of Mordor who are going after the people who took down their master, Sauron. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SDjEtbJuMP0 The expansion takes players beyond Gorgoroth where they will "gather unlikely allies and uncover the secrets hidden in Mordor's forgotten corners." Players will visit three new regions: Heledhris, Parth Rhavas, and Nan Ogol. In those places, players can learn new skills and receive enhancements, and then mix and match them to create a unique playstyle. The Wolves of Mordor expansion also adds new companions called Neighbors, who have their own unique personality traits and a "dynamic mood system." Players can forge friendships with these companions, and the companions can tell the player stories, provide gifts, and send them on missions. The Wolves of Mordor is available in a $40 standard edition, an $80 Collector's Edition with extra cosmetics, and the $130 Ultimate Fan Bundle. This version comes with even more cosmetics, additional neighbor characters, and XP boosts, among other things. The Lord of the Rings Online has added more than a dozen expansions since it was first released in 2007. The developer Turbine created the game, which began as a subscription-based MMO before pivoting to free-to-play in 2010. Warner Bros. originally published the game, but it changed hands to Daybreak Game Company, with development shifting to Standing Stone Games. The Lord of the Rings Online has been up and running for nearly 20 years, but it's not the longest-running MMO out there. gamespot.com/articles/fortnite-is-about-.excerpt: Fortnite's very last new collaboration for this year's Halloween season is with Predator: Badlands, and it includes the first Predator skin that's ever been available outside the permanently locked Chapter 2 Season 5 battle pass. But the main attraction in this set may actually be the back bling, which is the top half of Thia , the Weyland-Yutani android, played by Elle Fanning, who spends most of the movie strapped to the protagonist's back. The whole Predator: Badlands set hits the Fortnite shop on October 28 at 5 PM PT / 8 PM ET. It's exactly what fans of Dan Trachtenberg's film have hoped for since the collab was first announced last month. We knew a new Yautja (the in-universe name for the Predator species) skin was on the way, but it wasn't until the cosmetics were granted to content creators on Wednesday that we knew about the Thia back bling. In the film, a damaged Thia, torn in half on a hostile planet by a legendary alien beast called the Kalisk, teams up with a young Yautja called Dek in order to survive the monsters and other, more insidious threats that are hanging around the place. Since Thia spends much of the movie on Dek's back, she makes perfect sense to include as a back bling. Still, she's an extremely unusual one--it's only the second time we've had a human-shaped body as a back bling, after the similar C-3PO one from 2024, and it's the one of only three back blings that use a real person's likeness, after the Lil Tecca plushie and the Tyler the Creator doll . The Thia back bling is tagged as being reactive, which means it should move or make some kind of noise in response to things you do during a match. But it may be bugged right now, because these cosmetics have already been granted to content creators, like PIZ0 and VALtheVAL , and it doesn't seem to do anything in videos that those folks have posted so far. gamespot.com/articles/wow-forever-conten.title: WoW: Forever Content Updates Will Come Slower Than You Might Expect
gamespot.com/articles/wow-forever-conten.excerpt: Developer Blizzard's new version of its flagship MMORPG, World of Warcraft: Forever , will receive content updates "every four months," avoiding modern WoW's somewhat controversial eight-week patch cycle. In an interview with IGN , Forever principal game designer Kris Zierhut revealed the content schedule plan and explained Blizzard's reasoning. He said WoW Classic's Season of Discovery received updates "way too fast," every  8-10 weeks. Since the launch of WoW's Dragonflight expansion in 2022, an eight-week update schedule is also what modern WoW operates on. Its more frequent patch schedule means there's always something new to do, but has been criticized by some players due to the buggy nature of recent updates and lackluster content. https://youtu.be/9AlEQvn4dlc?si=JHSRubJ8HwfkO_Lw On the other hand, some older expansions, like Warlords of Draenor and Shadowlands, saw content droughts that lasted six months or more, leaving players hungry for something new to do. Forever will split the difference. "We're fairly convinced the correct [update] rate is something closer to once every four months or 17 weeks or three times a year," Zierhut said. Just because major updates will be coming every four or so months doesn't mean there won't be anything new to do between patches. Zierhut said some content will unlock partway through those four-month patch cycles. "It's not just patch day comes [around], here's a content fire hose, and now we're silent for four months," he said. "A lot of that is, 'Hey, there's a time event calendar that gradually unlocks things and opens them up over those four months' to give things a little bit more life instead of all at once." According to a Forever content roadmap released during BlizzCon 2026, the latest version of Blizzard's MMORPG will receive its first major update in Spring 2027. gamespot.com/articles/sleeping-dogs-movi.title: Sleeping Dogs Movie Director Explains Why The Adaptation Is Taking So Long
gamespot.com/articles/sleeping-dogs-movi.excerpt: Like many video game movies , Sleeping Dogs seems stuck in development hell. Even though it looked like progress on this adaptation of the cult-classic action game was once again picking up when Shang-Chi star Simu Liu started teasing new developments last year, and Timo Tjahjanto (Nobody 2) was later announced as the director , there's been little word since on whether the film will ever get off the ground. What's taking so long? According to Tjahjanto, the slow approach is by design. "Trust me when I say Simu and I are doing our best to slowly make this come into fruition," Tjahjanto wrote on X/Twitter . "Trying to stay as loyal to Wei Shen's tale while adding layers to make the narrative more fitting into a feature film is not an easy task. We're taking our time to make the best version of [Sleeping Dogs] the movie." Sleeping Dogs Sleeping Dogs isn't exactly a complex story, as the 2012 game saw undercover cop Wei Shen's loyalties tested after he infiltrated a Hong Kong triad and found himself in the middle of a gangland civil war. It's a fairly standard tale for a game inspired by Hong Kong action movies, unless Tjahjanto is trying to weave in the DLC's story, which introduced an undead army and magical tea. Sleeping Dogs is hardly the first video game adaptation to simmer in the background, as dozens of other projects are currently in varying stages of development. One notable example is the Ghost of Tsushima movie, which Chad Stahelski has been attached to direct for several years now; last we heard, Stahelski said a script was ready . That was in 2023, and with the John Wick director currently working on finishing up the new Highlander movie starring Henry Cavill, don't expect to see Jin Sakai in the live-action flesh anytime soon--at least an anime adaptation of the popular samurai open-world game will land in 2028.

Minecraft and WoW Forever set records, Call of Duty had its most acclaimed release in more than a decade, and our PC platform revenue grew double digits. Console sales remain constrained by supply, with more demand than consoles available. We're working to get more consoles into players’ hands, including through our expanded refurbishment program." https://twitter.com/asha_shar/status/2115574497621463499 In June, Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball also argued there was a supply-side issue with Xbox Series X|S . "We are producing them as quickly as possible," Ball said at the time. "These is a severe limitation to how quickly we can do that, but it’s not a question of appetite." Circana senior director Mat Piscatella expressed skepticism about Sharma's console-supply argument on Bluesky , noting that "the data I've seen do not suggest that stock has been the biggest driver of Xbox hardware performance." In addition, Xbox Series X|S hardware sales continue to crater in the US , setting new record lows for Microsoft's gaming brand. gamespot.com/articles/gta-6s-landmass-is.title: GTA 6’s Landmass Is Nearly As Big As GTA 4, GTA 5, And Red Dead Redemption 2 Combined
gamespot.com/articles/gta-6s-landmass-is.excerpt: GTA 6 has a big map, but just how big? According to Rockstar, the GTA 6 map is roughly twice the size of GTA 5's and three times the size of Red Dead Redemption 2's . The total landmass in GTA 6, however, is nearly as big as the playable maps for GTA 4, GTA 5, and Red Dead Redemption 2 combined , the developer told Edge magazine . GTA 6 is a large game in terms of its map and playable areas, but it's also dense, Rockstar says. Co-studio head Aaron Garbut said the game features an "order of magnitude more interiors" than any previous Rockstar game. "Every back alley is as densely detailed and interesting as the others. You can go anywhere, any random location, and so many people have thought about that location," he said, adding that there are places in GTA 6 that he himself has not personally seen yet, despite working on the game for years. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ILXsBB3UwSQ Also in the interview, Garbut talked about the pressure to deliver with GTA 6. After all, fans have been waiting 13 years and are expecting a lot. "We can't just trot out something that's what people might expect, or that was the easy thing to do," he said. "We've not compromised on the scale, the detail, the interactivity, the story, the open world. I feel like we've built a pyramid on Everest." GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game's file size is absolutely massive , and that makes sense given what Rockstar is saying about the size of the map. Additionally, GTA 6 Online could release in 2027 .

gamespot.com/articles/dead-space-meets-b.title: Dead Space Meets Back To The Future In This Terrifying Horror Game, And It’s Cheaper Than Ever
gamespot.com/articles/dead-space-meets-b.excerpt: After the brilliance of the Silent Hill 2 remake, all eyes were on Bloober Team for the next horror game the developer would dream (nightmare?) up. Thankfully, we didn’t have to wait too long, with Cronos: The New Dawn , an original IP, releasing the following year. With an atmosphere like Dead Space, strategic combat like Alan Wake, and time-travel shenanigans that Marty McFly would be able to handle, this is an under-loved horror gem that should be in your library in time for Halloween—and fortunately, it’s cheaper than ever right now. In Cronos, you play as the lovingly named Traveler ND-3576. Following the Change, which turned humans into monsters called Orphans, you work for an organization called the Collective, finding time-travel points that take you back to 1980s Poland in the hope of finding and extracting people who didn’t survive. Because working for a mysterious organization has never, ever gone wrong. With a suit taken straight from a ’60s sci-fi movie, the Traveler (and, in effect, you) will have to slowly walk through spooky, run-down buildings, finding resources and eventually fighting off Orphans. While they’re not Necromorphs, the Orphans look like a more violent take on the monster from The Thing, and in reality, they fight just as hard. Unsurprisingly, the suit the Traveler is wearing isn’t very nimble. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zCRGMkIRrwQ Cronos works so well because it oozes the intense, dread-inducing atmosphere that makes horror games so effective. Every corner feels like it could be hiding a monster, and that fear makes every level feel like a nightmarish experience. Considering how big of a hit Silent Hill 2’s remake was, I’m surprised I don’t see more conversation around Cronos because, for all intents and purposes, it’s like a sci-fi take on the beloved horror franchise. Just with slightly more body horror for good measure. If you’re looking to break the timelines and mess with the fate of the universe, all while dealing with horr

gamespot.com/articles/south-park-gives-u.title: South Park Gives Us A First Look At GTA 6’s Most Disgusting Feature
gamespot.com/articles/south-park-gives-u.excerpt: Did you know that you can throw dog poop at NPCs in Grand Theft Auto 6 ? While we've known about this feature for a while, we finally got a chance to see it in disgusting action thanks to this week's episode of South Park. For the last couple of weeks, the running gag in South Park--or South America, following its cheeky rebranding--is that all of society's woes will be solved once GTA 6 hits the scene, and the new episode continued that joke with an exclusive look at the game, which revealed some very important new facts. https://youtu.be/_8syp1jZxkY There are dedicated animations of dogs taking a poop The NPCs who own that dog will then collect its droppings You can attack the NPC, by picking up the dog poop and smashing it in their faces Yes, the poop does explode into smaller, messy chunks on impact Beyond this season's GTA 6 jokes, South Park has made numerous video game references over the years. The most famous is Season 10's Make Love, Not Warcraft, which focused entirely on Blizzard's World of Warcraft MMO. That 2006 episode featured a ton of machinima animation pulled directly from WoW, crafted by Blizzard by using a selection of in-game footage and character models. Since then, South Park has also referenced Nintendo, and a 2019 two-episode storyline heavily referenced Rockstar's Red Dead Redemption 2. In related news, GTA 6 is already breaking records before it's even out, and the game is going to be a massive download --fortunately, you'll have a week to grab it. The entertainment industry is also preparing for what will likely be the biggest video game launch of all time, as the director of the new Hunger Games movie, Francis Lawrence, hopes people can find time to watch the film when it launches a day after GTA 6. EA founder Bing Gordon also believes GTA 6 will succeed if people choose to play the game instead of watching football when Thanksgiving weekend kicks off a few days after launch.

rockpapershotgun.com/gta-6-has-a-smell-r.title: GTA 6 has a smell reaction system, which immediately joins Red Dead Redemption 2's dynamically shrinking horse balls on Rockstar's list of immersive symbols of excess
rockpapershotgun.com/gta-6-has-a-smell-r.excerpt: Any reminder of Red Dead Redemption 2 's temperature sensitive horse testicles brings a smile to my face. In truth, I can't say I've ever zoomed in close enough to properly take in the spectacle of Arthur Morgan's mount having its nuts dynamically expand and contract based on whether he's riding through snowy mountains or across baking plains, but I do always get a kick out of knowing such a thing's happening as I play. To this point, the horse balls have been the most infamous or meme-worthy example of Rockstar's obsession with going all-in on realistic detail to an arguably unnecessary degree, one that borders on overindulgence which players could conceivably never notice if they weren't expressly told about it. That philosophy's gone nowhere, so GTA 6 was always going to have a feature that'd become as much of a metaphor for excess as those beloved balls. gamespot.com/articles/dont-expect-destin.title: Don’t Expect Destiny 3 At The Game Awards, Bungie Says
gamespot.com/articles/dont-expect-destin.excerpt: Destiny's future lies in its past, as Bungie is working to bring content from the infamous Destiny vault back to the game. Big plans are in place to rework fan-favorite campaigns like the Red War and Forsaken back into Destiny 2 , and while that content won't be out for quite a while, Bungie has also detailed what you should not expect from the studio as the year winds down. Long story short: Don't expect to see Destiny 3 teased at The Game Awards. "Knowing we are early in incubating our future and actively working on projects to bridge us to that new home, don't expect us to make a Destiny announcement at the TGAs this year, or to randomly drop a logo that sets the world on fire right away," head of product Josh Deane wrote . Bungie says it secured an "initial greenlight to begin scoping the work" back in June, and a yet-to-be-revealed studio will help with its Destiny legacy content revival. To keep fans up to date, the studio has unveiled a progress bar, with which will signal when major milestones have been reached: The new Destiny 2 progress bar. "Right now, we are in our pre-production, proof-of-work stage where we will ensure the process is working and hitting our quality bar as we port the legacy content. We expect this part of the process to last until roughly January/February. From that point we expect full production will be about 12 months. to fully complete the porting process. It’s a lot of content," Deane added. What else is on the Destiny horizon? Deane said that players can look forward to "anchor" events, like a new celebration in Destiny 2 similar to Moments of Triumph, and Destiny Legacy, which Deane described as being "the whole experience" that needs to be served to where players are today. While the wording was vague, it sounds as if Destiny 1 content might come to Destiny 2. gamespot.com/articles/my-mom-became-a-cr.title: “My Mom Became A Crater” Is A Very Death Stranding Way To Start An Anime
gamespot.com/articles/my-mom-became-a-cr.excerpt: The first trailer for the Death Stranding anime spin-off, Death Stranding: Isolations, has dropped, revealing a quick and spooky glimpse at a world that has been ravaged by several extinction events. The brief teaser reveals little, and amusingly, the official synopsis simply reads, "My mom became a crater." But if you are a fan of Hideo Kojima's post-apocalyptic world and setting? There's plenty to glean from this footage through the visuals, and the trailer also reveals the talent behind this project. https://youtu.be/ruIT6Xez6tw If you're unfamiliar with the games, Death Stranding takes place in a world where humanity has been brought to the brink of extinction. After Beached Things (BTs) began to roam the land, various cataclysms broke out across the world. BTs would arise via necrosis from deceased humans, and if they made contact with living people, that would result in massive "voidout" explosions that could easily wipe out a city. To make matters worse, BTs are also the root cause of Timefall, a rain that rapidly ages anything it hits, which eventually led the surviving populace to form Knot Cities across the USA, which was subsequently renamed to the United Cities of America. Death Stranding: Isolations tells an original story within that setting, and it follows a young girl living in a voidout crater--possibly the one caused by her mom, as the trailer suggests. "In the wake of this cataclysm, many were forced to live in absolute isolation--among them, a young girl. Although this lonely existence was forced upon her, she soon grows to prefer solitude, eschewing all opportunities for real human connection and allowing herself to be strung along by fate," the synopsis reads. The series also has notable talent attached, including director Takayuki Sano (Jujutsu Kaisen). The crew also includes writer Tow Ubukata (Psycho-Pass), character designers Ilya Kuvshinov (Ghost in the Shell: SAC 2045) and Sayaka Koiso (Dorohedoro), and Death Stranding creator Hideo Kojim

gamespot.com/articles/everything-new-in-.excerpt: One Piece is taking over Fortnite for the next month as part of the game's now-annual November mini-season, which swaps out the current Battle Royale island for a smaller new pirate-themed one. Dubbed Fortnite Treasure Hunters, the new season starts November 1 and will also focus heavily on music collabs with A$AP Rocky, Lil Uzi Vert, Hatsune Miku and Kasane Teto--Epic isn't putting all its eggs in one cartoon basket like it did last year with its Simpsons season. Epic started doing these mini-seasons back in Chapter 4 with the original Fortnite OG event, and that one went so well that the company decided to make it a tradition. With Fortnite facing down the launch of GTA VI in late November, it needed some serious firepower--and One Piece, which has been one of the most requested Fortnite collabs ever, certainly qualifies. Let's take a look at the details. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rFHOT4Mb_yI Fortnite Treasure Hunters battle pass The Treasure Hunters battle pass is not a full collab pass, unlike the Simpsons and Star Wars ones from 2025. Instead, the pass includes three anime-themed Fortnite people and two One Piece characters--Nico Robin and Portgas D. Ace. The rest of the rather robust roster of One Piece skins will be in the shop, which we'll talk about later. The Fortnite original characters in the pass include anime makeovers of Jonesy and Syd, as well as a rare re-do of Charlotte from the Chapter 2 Season 8 battle pass. Welcome to Skull Island (sort of) The current BR island is being replaced with Crossbones Isle, a smaller island that has a max capacity of 80 players, down from the usual 100--same as the Springfield map last year. The new map has a lot more water than the Chapter 7 map did, and it's filled with new locations based on One Piece, like Arlong Park and Windmill Village, as well as spots based on the music collabs. gamespot.com/articles/hellraiser-revival.title: Hellraiser: Revival Is A Brutal, Gory Gift You Should Get Yourself This Halloween
gamespot.com/articles/hellraiser-revival.excerpt: If I had a nickel for every time an ’80s British horror movie got turned into a successful and faithful horror game almost four decades later, I wouldn’t have a lot of nickels. In fact, I’d probably have only one—thanks to Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival . It’s gross, brutal, and as horrific as you’ve come to expect from the franchise, but you don’t need to know Hellraiser to enjoy it. In fact, going in blind is an interesting experience, and right now, you can get a huge discount on it for a limited time. You play as Aidan, who chases extreme situations during the “fun” times with his girlfriend, as the pair accidentally summon the demonic Cenobites thanks to the familiar Genesis Configuration. (If I had a nickel for every time that happened to me… I wouldn’t have any.) After being knocked unconscious and becoming a captive of the Scarlet Church, Aidan fights against the cult’s desire to activate the Rite of Rebirth and attempts to find his girlfriend. In familiar “ horror game protagonist” fashion, Aidan isn’t some soldier armed to the teeth with weapons and ammunition. You’re no Arnold in Predator, so to speak. Instead, most of the game requires melee combat, meaning you’ll need to get close to your enemies and whammy them with clunky attacks. While that clunkiness would normally be a negative, Hellraiser: Revival’s atmosphere, combined with Aidan’s lack of fighting skills, makes each fight feel more like a struggle for survival than an action sequence. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0rA40lqttO8 I’ll be honest: Even as a horror fanatic, Hellraiser: Revival is uncomfortable at the best of times. Between intense gore that will make even the most steadfast squirm and brutal combat that will make your skin crawl, it’s not for the sensitive—or even those who are fairly comfortable with a bit of grossness. gamespot.com/articles/what-gta-clones-di.title: What GTA Clones Did Better Than Grand Theft Auto Itself
gamespot.com/articles/what-gta-clones-di.excerpt: Grand Theft Auto represents the pinnacle of AAA games, not just in huge-scale production values, but in the kind of innovation that rewrites the rules for what games can even be. It seems only Rockstar is capable of fully nailing this style of game. Of course, with its level of success, that hasn't stopped other developers from trying. Rightly or wrongly, these games are often dubbed GTA clones, a label that automatically assumes it's an inferior imitation to the real McCoy. However, that doesn't mean these games don't have their redeeming features and innovations that offer something different, or in some cases, even arguably improves on GTA's shortcomings--yes, even one of the greatest game series of all time is imperfect. Even as GTA 6 promises to be the most refined vision of open-world gaming that eclipses all the competition, there's still a good chance you'll find some feature in these clones that’s more compelling than Rockstar's own criminal paradise. Mafia (2002) Mafia (Definitive Edition) "Open-world game" for many players means having the freedom to explore and do whatever you want within a large sandbox. However, Mafia's Lost Heaven was very much a "faux-pen world" that served as one large movie set you'd just drive around from mission to mission. While that might sound like a criticism, it worked in favor for Czech developer Illusion Softworks and its atmospheric period piece set in 1930s America. In taking a more mature and serious direction, Mafia was also more realistic in many ways, from the real-time damage of vehicles to a more in-depth minor- and serious-offense system from the cops compared to GTA's star-based Wanted System. It may not appeal to players looking for a sandbox for wanton criminal chaos, but when it comes to telling the story of a humble man's rise and fall in the world of crime, and the ultimate consequences, few games do it as memorably. gamespot.com/articles/ea-just-shelved-a-.excerpt: It's been another rough year for video games, with countless studio closures, staff layoffs, and projects that barely managed to even get off the ground before they were unceremoniously cut short . But things are feeling especially grim after EA trotted out two beloved franchises--Mass Effect and Dragon Age--for what amounted to a public execution via the announcement that BioWare has been shuttered . This was especially painful for Mass Effect players, who were looking forward to the upcoming Mass Effect 5, which we now know was tentatively titled Mass Effect: Universe. But it's not just BioWare fans who are upset at the moment. Fans of EA's other properties are growing increasingly concerned about the future of those franchises, if any future is planned for them at all. My colleague Levi Winslow recently wrote about their concerns for the Skate franchise in the wake of layoffs at its development studio. Meanwhile, I'm quite worried about the fate of The Sims. But everyone knows that when it comes to profits, EA's sports titles outrun its other IPs by a country mile. gamespot.com/articles/cod-modern-warfare.title: CoD: Modern Warfare To Cut Real-Life Korean Tragedy Segment After Backlash
gamespot.com/articles/cod-modern-warfare.excerpt: Publisher Activision has responded to criticism over using a devastating tragedy in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , saying that the incident will be removed from the military shooter in a November 12 update. The Seoul Halloween crowd crush occurred in October 2022 in Itaewon. Approximately 100,000 people gathered in a narrow alleyway in Seoul, resulting in 160 casualties as people were suffocated. This year marks the fourth anniversary of the tragedy, with bereaved families and community organizers gathering to remember the lives that were lost. Modern Warfare 4 hit consoles and PC on October 23, and not long after its release, the game drew criticism from bereaved Korean families. In the opening cutscene to the game's campaign--which focuses on a fictional war between North and South Korea--Modern Warfare 4 depicts a chaotic scene where one person performs CPR on a downed individual, while bodies are either laid out on the streets or carried away on stretchers. Given the game's setting and the events on screen, the 10.29 Itaewon Disaster Bereaved Families Association and the Citizens' Countermeasures Meeting--two organizations formed after the 2022 tragedy in Seoul--were "appalled" at the calamity's inclusion and demanded that Activision remove it from the game. "Using such an incident as material for a game intended for entertainment purposes is itself highly inappropriate and a senseless act," the groups said, according to the BBC . "The Itaewon tragedy was a tragic disaster that produced hundreds of casualties, and citizens who participated in the rescue efforts or witnessed the event at the time continue to suffer from trauma. If the game developer has even a minimum level of courtesy and empathy toward the victims, they should promptly take corrective measures." Activision has heard the call and plans to remove the depiction from Modern Warfare 4 when an update arrives on November 12. gamespot.com/articles/phantom-blade-zero.excerpt: There's a new voice behind the protagonist of Soul in Phantom Blade Zero , and it's none other than Sonic the Hedgehog--or his longtime voice actor, Roger Craig Smith, to be precise. As spotted by Game Informer , Smith has stepped in to replace Jay Maksenuk (V in Once Human). You can still hear the latter in the various trailers for Phantom Blade Zero, and developer S-Game hasn't revealed why they brought Smith on as a last-minute replacement. Both actors have several video game credits, and as Game Informer noted, it sounds like Masenuk was replaced shortly after the game's review period began. Essentially, you won't be hearing Masenuk's voice, as the game launched earlier this week with Craig voicing the main character. You're probably familiar with Craig's voice; in addition to Sonic and Batman, he's also voiced Ezio Auditore in several Assassin's Creed games, Daigo Dojima in Yakuza Kiwami 3, and Alden Dorne in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7. nintendolife.com/news/2026/10/digital-fo.title: Digital Foundry Delivers Its Tech Verdict On Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 On Switch 2
nintendolife.com/news/2026/10/digital-fo.excerpt: Is it really all that 'Modern'? Just in case the news passed you by, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launched on Switch 2 this month — the first in the series to do so since the Wii U days. Naturally, a lot of the attention has been on the game's performance and whether the Switch 2 would be able to keep up with its competitors. Here to answer exactly that are the tech experts over at Digital Foundry , who have just shared their thoughts on the hybrid version's nitty-gritty details. We'll start with the all-important frame rates. DF states that MW4 runs at 30fps in its campaign mode, 60fps in competitive multiplayer, and 40fps (if you have a 120Hz display hooked up) in the DMZ extraction mode. While this is a little lower than other platforms — particularly in the campaign respect — it does mean that we Switch 2 players can still get the full-fat CoD experience.
